query_text: Is it time for schools to replace the teaching of foreign languages with instruction in computer coding languages?

Based on my research, this is a complex and actively debated question in education policy worldwide. Here's what the evidence shows:

## The Case for Coding Education

There's no doubt that coding education is expanding rapidly in schools globally. Several countries are making significant commitments:

- **India (CBSE)**: Starting in 2026-27, AI and Computational Thinking will be introduced from Class 3 onwards, becoming compulsory in Classes 9-10 (https://makersmuse.in/news/cbses-big-move-ai-coding-from-class-3-what-schools-teachers-need-to-know-in-2026/)
- **Indonesia**: Coding and AI will be implemented as elective subjects starting from the 2025/2026 academic year, beginning in fourth grade (https://en.tempo.co/read/1940956/coding-ai-subjects-to-be-implemented-in-elementary-schools-in-academic-year-of-20252026-minister)
- **Egypt**: Expanding coding and AI education to technical schools in 2026/27, building on a program that already enrolled 236,000 general secondary students (https://iafrica.com/egypt-to-expand-ai-and-coding-curriculum-to-technical-schools-starting-in-2026/)
- **Ireland**: Launched coding in primary schools in 2018 with computer programming as a Leaving Certificate subject, aiming to make Irish education the best in Europe by 2026 (https://hiberniacollege.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/Hibernia-College-Education-Papers-2.pdf)

Tech industry leaders like Tim Cook have called coding "the most important second language," and the job market demand for programming skills continues to grow.

## Why Most Experts Say Replacement Is a Mistake

However, the consensus among educators and linguists is that **coding should complement, not replace, foreign language education**. Here are the key arguments:

### 1. Fundamental Differences Between "Languages"

Computer coding and human languages are fundamentally different in nature. As one expert explains:

- **Foreign languages** (humanities): Systems "of words or signs that people use to express thoughts and feelings to each other" — tied to culture, history, and human society
- **Programming languages** (science/engineering): "A formal system of signs and symbols including rules for the formation and transformation of admissible expressions" — instructions for computers (https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dont-swap-coding-classes-foreign-language-igor-perisic)

### 2. Cultural Competency Cannot Be Replaced

Modern language education serves crucial humanistic goals that coding cannot fulfill. The Modern Language Association emphasizes that language learning builds:

- Cultural awareness and reduced ethnocentrism
- Understanding of different values, communicative norms, and social practices
- Perspective-taking abilities essential for a just society (https://linguisticpulse.com/2014/02/03/computer-code-human-language-why-coding-cant-replace-language-education/)

As one analysis notes, there are at least 100 ways to say "I" in Japanese — each revealing something profound about how selfhood is constructed in relation to others. No programming language offers this kind of cultural insight (https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/dont-swap-coding-classes-foreign-language-igor-perisic).

### 3. Practical Career Considerations

While computer science offers high-paying jobs, foreign language skills remain broadly applicable across all fields. As one commentator notes: "Being able to speak another language increasingly helps recent graduates get good-paying jobs and then advance more rapidly in them" (https://thebablueprint.com/7937/opinion/coding-should-replace-foreign-language/).

### 4. The "Both/And" Approach

Most education reformers advocate for **adding** coding to curricula rather than **substituting** it for languages. The CBSE reforms in India exemplify this: they're adding AI/coding while also strengthening language requirements (two Indian languages plus English) (https://sunbeamworldschool.com/blog/cbse-new-curriculum-2026-27/).

## Legislative Attempts and Their Fate

Some U.S. states have proposed allowing coding to satisfy foreign language requirements:
- **Florida**: A bill passed the state Senate but died in the House (https://www.unitedlanguagegroup.com/learn/global-news/teaching-coding-foreign-language)
- **Kentucky** and **New Mexico**: Similar proposals emerged but faced significant opposition

These proposals have largely failed because they conflate superficial similarities (vocabulary, syntax) while ignoring profound differences in purpose and outcome.

## Conclusion

**No, it is not time to replace foreign languages with coding.** The better approach — increasingly adopted worldwide — is to integrate both into expanded curricula. Coding builds computational thinking and technical skills; foreign languages build cultural competency, communication flexibility, and human understanding. Both are essential for 21st-century education, but they serve different, non-interchangeable purposes.

The real challenge is not choosing between them, but ensuring schools have adequate resources, teacher training, and time to teach both effectively.
